papers.title: Exploring the Effectiveness of Cyberbullying Awareness Training in Middle School Students: A Randomized Controlled Trial
papers.abstract: Background: Cyberbullying, which occurs when information and communication technologies are used to harm individuals, is one of the most important problems for adolescents today. This study evaluated the effectiveness of nurse-led cyberbullying awareness training for 7th-grade middle school students. Results: It was determined that the control and intervention groups had a homogeneous distribution in terms of demographic characteristics. In terms of their pre-test and post-test mean scores on the CAS, there was no statistically significant difference between the control and intervention groups (P > .05). However, within the control group, a statistically significant difference was found between the pre-training and post-training CAS scores (Z = −2.890; P = .004 < .05). In contrast, the intervention group showed no statistically significant difference between their pre-training and post-training CAS scores (P > .05). Conclusions: This study evaluated the effects of nurse-led training program aimed at increasing cyberbullying awareness. Comprehensive and long-term awareness programs led by nurses are likely to produce more lasting and effective outcomes for young individuals.

papers.title: Does a one-week disability awareness training influence medical students attitudes? A French mixed-methods study.
papers.abstract:
BACKGROUND
Disability is experienced by approximately 1.3 billion individuals worldwide. Therefore, people with disabilities (PWD) are part of every physician's patient base, regardless of specialty. Specific educational programs are needed, as medical students and physicians still report discomfort in taking histories, performing clinical examinations and making differential diagnoses when dealing with PWD.


OBJECTIVE
We hypothesized that participation in a one-week disability awareness training, including theoretical sessions, practical workshops with PWD, and 3-day immersive training courses, would significantly improve the quantitative and qualitative outcomes of medical students toward PWD.


METHODS
We conducted a monocentric prospective mixed-methods study targeting 3rd year medical students, using quantitative measurements through repeated synchronous surveys, evaluating disability attitudes in health care (DAHC) scores and performed qualitative explorations through individual semidirected interviews, evaluating students' feelings and attitudes toward PWD.


RESULTS
A total of 218 students (mean age: 21.1 ± 1.4 years) were included in the study. While 60 % of the participants reported no prior working experience with PWD, there was a significant improvement in paired-DAHC scores 3 months after the training (+1.32, p = 0.003). Improvements were predominantly observed in comfort levels during interaction and in discriminatory attitudes. This practical experience was positively reported in the semidirected interviews, in which a facilitated transition from unfamiliarity to informed empathy and knowledge was reported.


CONCLUSIONS
The implementation of disability awareness trainings in compulsory medical curricula should be prioritized to improve future physician's skills and attitudes when caring for PWD.

papers.title: Ai-Driven Cybersecurity Awareness Training (CSAT) Framework
papers.abstract: Human error continues to be a prevailing cause of cybersecurity attacks, and it necessitates immediate responsive and personal training solutions. Conventional Cybersecurity Awareness Training (CSAT) schemes are generally contextually irrelevant, lack scalability, and are missing ongoing risk assessment. The paper will mitigate such shortcomings by suggesting a multi-phase CSAT model whereby Generative Artificial Intelligence (GAI), online machine learning algorithms, and MITRE ATT&CK- based threat models are incorporated to provide rolespecific and threat-sensitive delivery of cybersecurity education. The framework includes realtime user profiling, vulnerability analysis and a machine learning pipeline that includes Random Forest with Recursive Feature Elimination, Isolation Forest, K-Means clustering and Decision Trees to find out risks based on behavior. The dynamically generated training content is based on weaknesses that are unique to the users and the changing risk profiles between the users. Simulated organizational profiles with experimental evaluation indicate that there were significant changes of Risk Scores and Vulnerability Scores among partici-ants. This confirms the model as effective in increasing the awareness of the users, alleviating behavioral weaknesses, and facilitating ongoing learning. The suggested framework provides flexible and smart approach to reinforcing organizational cybersecurity postures and providing quantifiable and specific outcomes.

papers.title: The Role of Awareness Training in Recognising Child Neglect and Abuse Among Health‐Care Professionals
papers.abstract:
Structured awareness training significantly improves health‐care professionals' ability to recognise and respond to child neglect and abuse.
 
 
 Continuous, multidisciplinary and interactive training supports early identification, mandatory reporting and effective child protection.
 
 
 Evaluation results showed measurable improvements in all awareness areas, underlining the importance of regular, practice‐based training in safeguarding children.

papers.title: IoT-Specific Cybersecurity Awareness Training (CSAT) Framework
papers.abstract: The widespread adoption of Internet of Things (IoT) and Operational Technology (OT) sys- tems in industrial environments has significantly in- creased cybersecurity exposure. Human error re- mains a leading cause of successful cyberattacks; how- ever, conventional Cybersecurity Awareness Training (CSAT) programs are typically static and poorly aligned with user roles, asset criticality, and evolving threats. This paper proposes an IoT-focused risk- adaptive CSAT framework that integrates MITRE ATT&CK-based threat modeling, CIA-aware impact analysis, machine learning-driven risk assessment, and Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI) for person- alized training delivery. The framework models cyber- security awareness as a continuous closed-loop process that constructs user-specific attack graphs, evaluates vulnerabilities through adaptive assessments, and com- putes local and global risk scores. Machine learning dynamically derives risk thresholds to guide training prioritization, while GenAI generates targeted training content aligned with real-world attack scenarios. Evaluation using representative industrial user profiles demonstrates consistent reductions in vulnerability and global risk levels following personalized training. The results indicate that the proposed framework has the potential to enhance human-centric security and im- prove the effectiveness of cybersecurity awareness pro- grams in industrial IoT environments.

papers.title: Subliminal beauty engages the brain's valuation circuits.
papers.abstract: Neuroeconomic models propose that the anterior ventral striatum (aVS) and ventromedial prefrontal cortex (vmPFC) are key regions for computing subjective value (SV) signals that guide choice. However, the role of conscious awareness in this process remains debated. Here we examined whether SV can be automatically computed in these regions without conscious awareness. In an fMRI experiment, human participants (24 females, 5 males) viewed faces that varied in attractiveness under three conditions: (i) suppressed from awareness via continuous flash suppression (CFS), (ii) clearly visible without suppression, or (iii) absent (background only) with CFS. Participants reported trial-wise facial identity (objective) and visibility (subjective) measures of facial awareness. In a post-fMRI session, they rated the attractiveness of each face as a measure of SV. When faces were seen, task performance (d') exceeded chance and responses were faster than in absent trials. When faces were unseen, performance was at chance but responses were slower than absent trials. Neurally, seen and unseen faces elicited greater neural signal than absent trials and showed similar neural patterns in the fusiform face area (FFA). Critically, neural signal in vmPFC correlated with SV for both seen and unseen faces, with similar neural patterns. In aVS, SV-related signal was only observed for unseen faces. Furthermore, mean face-related signal in FFA correlated with SV-related signals in aVS and vmPFC for unseen faces. These findings demonstrate that SV can be automatically computed in aVS and vmPFC without conscious awareness, suggesting a neural pathway by which subliminal information can influence value-based choice.

papers.title: Impacts of Nature-Based Interventions on Healthcare Workers' Stress, Burnout, and Performance: A Systematic Literature Review.
papers.abstract: ObjectivesThis systematic review synthesizes evidence on the efficacy of nature-based interventions (NBIs) in mitigating stress and burnout among healthcare workers (HCWs) while enhancing their performance.BackgroundWork-related stress and burnout are major challenges among HCWs, with adverse impacts on HCWs' well-being, patient outcomes, and healthcare systems. Although behavioral and organizational interventions have been widely studied, less attention has been given to NBIs, despite growing evidence of their potential for stress reduction.MethodThis review synthesized findings from 20 empirical studies published through October 2024, examining the types of NBIs used in healthcare settings and their effects on HCWs' stress, burnout, and performance. Following the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses guidelines, studies were identified across four NBI domains: outdoor activity in nature, virtual reality, real-world sensory stimulation (e.g., nature-themed recharge rooms, natural sounds), and visual access to nature.ResultsNBIs consistently reduced psychological and physiological stress. Evidence for burnout reduction was mixed, with the most evident effects in reducing exhaustion and depersonalization, but insignificant impacts on personal accomplishment. Performance-related outcomes such as mindfulness, resilience, and cognitive functions were generally enhanced, with immersive exposure to natural elements yielding stronger effects.ConclusionOverall, NBIs demonstrated promising results in reducing HCWs' stress and improving performance outcomes, but the impact on burnout was limited. Practical applications should consider feasibility and sustainability. Design strategies may include outdoor green spaces, such as rooftop gardens or courtyards, as well as passive indoor features that provide continuous restorative benefits, including window views of nature, plants, and curated soundscapes.

papers.title: Interventions to improve wellbeing and job satisfaction among pharmacists: A systematic review.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Pharmacists experience substantial work-related stress and burnout, which may adversely affect their wellbeing and job satisfaction. However, evidence regarding interventions designed to improve these outcomes among pharmacists has not been systematically synthesised. This systematic review aimed to identify and evaluate interventions designed to improve wellbeing and job satisfaction of pharmacists. METHODS: Five electronic databases (PubMed, Embase, CINAHL, PsycINFO, and Scopus) were searched for studies evaluating interventions targeting wellbeing and/or job satisfaction in samples including pharmacists. Study selection, data extraction, and risk-of-bias assessment were conducted independently by two reviewers. Owing to heterogeneity in study designs, interventions, outcomes, and follow-up periods, findings were synthesised narratively. RESULTS: Seven studies were included in the final narrative analysis. The interventions included evaluating mindfulness-based programmes, resilience training, self-directed e-learning, gratitude letter writing, digital cognitive behavioural therapy, and job crafting. Most interventions were associated with improvements in at least one wellbeing-related outcome, including burnout, resilience, perceived stress, emotional distress, psychological wellbeing, and work-life balance. However, none of the studies exclusively recruited pharmacists, and pharmacist represented less than %10 which indicated a small number in several studies. Importantly, intervention outcomes were reported for overall multidisciplinary healthcare professional samples rather than separately for pharmacists. No included study evaluated job satisfaction as an outcome. Risk of bias ranged from some concerns to critical across studies. CONCLUSION: Available interventions show potential for improving wellbeing among healthcare professional populations that included pharmacists; however, their effectiveness specifically for pharmacists remains uncertain. Pharmacist-specific, high-quality intervention studies with longer follow-up are needed, particularly those evaluating job satisfaction and organisational-level strategies.

papers.title: Application of a Brief, Personality-Based Intervention for Borderline Personality Disorder for a Patient With Intersecting Identities: A BPD Compass Case Study.
papers.abstract: Borderline personality disorder (BPD) is a heterogeneous condition characterized by emotion dysregulation, interpersonal dysfunction, impulsivity, identity disturbance, and elevated rates of co-occurrence with other mental health conditions. Criterion B of the Alternative Model of Personality Disorders (AMPD) conceptualizes BPD symptoms as manifestations of dimensional personality traits, particularly negative affectivity, antagonism, and disinhibition. BPD Compass (Cognitive-behavioral Modules for Personality Symptoms) is an 18-session modular cognitive-behavioral intervention designed to target these higher-order personality dimensions and their underlying maintenance mechanisms. This article presents a detailed case study illustrating the application of BPD Compass with a 25-year-old bisexual Appalachian woman diagnosed with BPD, persistent depressive disorder, binge eating disorder, and subclinical social anxiety disorder. Treatment integrated values clarification, cognitive flexibility, behavioral skills, and mindfulness strategies tailored to the patient's cultural and identity-related experiences. Throughout treatment, interventions were personalized to address the impact of Appalachian cultural norms, minority stress related to sexual identity, emotional avoidance, interpersonal mistrust, and impulsive coping behaviors. By posttreatment, the patient demonstrated substantial reductions in BPD symptom severity, with Zanarini Rating Scale scores decreasing from 23 to 6. She no longer met criteria for binge eating disorder or clinically significant social anxiety symptoms and reported meaningful improvements in emotion regulation, interpersonal functioning, and impulse control.
